core_obligations: The adjoint properties (proof lines 8426-8427): the pushforward is a right adjoint, hence commutes with arbitrary limits and is left exact.

Faithfulness and reflection (proof lines 8427-8429): the canonically split surjection from the stalk of the pushforward onto the set implies faithfulness, reflection of injections, of surjections and of isomorphisms.

Surjections and coequalizers (proof lines 8430-8439): the point may be assumed to come from a point of the underlying site, in which case the pushforward is given by the display, from which the remaining two properties follow immediately.
proof_roadmap: Use the adjunction for limits and left exactness.
Use the split surjection for faithfulness and reflection properties.
Reduce to a point of the site and read off the last two properties from the formula.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects exactness properties of the pushforward along a point of a topos: it commutes with arbitrary limits, is left exact, faithful, transforms surjections into surjections, commutes with coequalizers, and reflects injections, surjections and isomorphisms (statement lines 8413-8423). The proof is a complete argument: the adjointness gives commutation with limits and left exactness (proof lines 8426-8427); the canonically split surjection from the stalk gives faithfulness and the reflection properties (proof lines 8427-8429); and after reducing to a point of the underlying site the author reads off the remaining two properties from the explicit formula for the pushforward (proof lines 8430-8439). The non-formal content is the use of the split surjection and of the formula. The claim is H1/H2: several short arguments with each input named.
